headline: Seasonal Peak Parking and Camping Management
reservation: Day-use parking may reach capacity on summer weekends, leading to temporary closures to new arrivals. Camping and glamping sites in and around Madison require advance reservations, especially for the mid-May through mid-October season. Check the official Connecticut State Parks portal for specific vehicle fee systems and site availability.

days.title: Coastal Nature and Discovery

stops.name: Meigs Point Nature Center
stops.detail: Learn about the local Long Island Sound ecosystem through interactive exhibits and touch tanks.

stops.name: Willard’s Island Trail
stops.detail: Walk through salt marshes to observe migratory birds and coastal flora.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; conditions vary by seasonal traffic
days.note: Insect repellent is recommended for marsh areas during summer afternoons.

days.title: Shoreline Recreation

stops.name: West Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the expansive sandy shoreline and swimming in the calm waters of the Sound.

stops.name: Shoreline Greenway Trail
stops.detail: Cycle or walk the paved path to see the park's interior habitats.

days.note: Arrive early during summer to ensure proximity to your preferred beach area.

days.title: Points and Piers

stops.name: Meigs Point Jetty
stops.detail: Explore the rocky shoreline during low tide for views across the Sound to Long Island.

stops.name: Hammonasset Fishing Pier
stops.detail: Observe local angling or try crabbing along the designated tidal inlets.

days.driving: Allow 35 minutes; conditions vary by I-95 traffic
days.note: Check local tide charts to maximize shoreline exploration at the rocky points.

intel.title: Peak Capacity Closures
intel.text: During hot summer weekends, lots often fill by 11 AM, and the park may close to all non-campers. Monitor official social media or DOT signs on I-95 for real-time status.

intel.title: Reliable Shoreline Coverage
intel.text: Mobile signal is generally strong throughout the park, including the main beaches and nature center. Some dead zones may exist in the deepest parts of the salt marshes.

intel.title: Gateway Amenities
intel.text: Full services including fuel and groceries are available in Madison and Clinton just minutes from the park gates. The park store inside the campground provides ice and basic essentials.

intel.title: Shoreline Morning Advantage
intel.text: Water conditions are typically calmest in the early morning, ideal for paddleboarding or walking the shoreline. Midday heat in July and August can be intense without ocean breezes.

intel.title: Non-Resident Fees
intel.text: Out-of-state vehicles are required to pay parking fees, while CT-registered vehicles may have fees waived via the Passport to the Parks. Confirm current payment methods at the gate.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Tweed New Haven (HVN) and stop for coastal supplies in Madison before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for paved park roads; RVs should check specific campground loop dimensions before booking.
plan.goldenHour: Meigs Point offers unobstructed western views over the Sound, providing excellent light during the late evening.
